The Financial Analyst Memo: every financial table and model output behind this memo

Volati: a levered trough recovery in which deleveraging, not a re-rating, does most of the work; the return arithmetic is attractive, the setup fits Richard's patterns poorly, and the balance sheet is fragile until the FY2026 report on 11 February 2027

Volati AB (VOLO-SE): investment memo, 8 November 2026. Price SEK 23.75 (23 October 2026). Market value about SEK 1.9bn on 79.4m ordinary shares. Continuing operations only, after the distribution of Salix Group on 15 June 2026. SEK m unless stated. The definitions of adjusted EBITA, adjusted EPS, reported EPS and leverage are in the end notes.

Warning: do not use the model summary's figures
The Financial Analyst's model summary (update 2) shows FY2027 EPS of SEK 6.11 and a total return of +272%; both figures are artefacts of three mechanical faults and must not be used. This memo uses the corrected forecasts, which the model reproduces once the three faults are fixed. The returns in #12 are indicative until the model is re-run. The end notes describe the faults and the corrected forecasts.

The decision in one paragraph. The return arithmetic is attractive, but the setup is not clean. Deleveraging and self-help, not end markets or sentiment, carry the base case to about SEK 40 a share at end-2027. A 30% chance of a bear case at about SEK 15 pulls the probability-weighted value down to about SEK 33 to 34, still roughly 40% above today's price. The balance sheet is fragile until the FY2026 report on 11 February 2027, so the practical question for Richard is how much of that fragile window to carry in exchange for a better entry price.

#0Summary: key insights, implications and conclusions

What Volati now is. Volati is now a SEK 1.9bn Swedish holding company of five unrelated platforms: Ettiketto (labels, about two-thirds of platform EBITA), Communication (masts and mounting hardware), Corroventa (water-damage drying, now including Tramex), S:t Eriks (precast concrete) and Tornum (grain handling). Three senior claims sit ahead of the ordinary equity: about SEK 1.33bn of net debt, SEK 0.4bn of leases and SEK 1.0bn of listed preference shares that cost SEK 64m a year. The ordinary equity is therefore only about 40% of an enterprise value of about SEK 4.6bn, and that thin slice magnifies everything in the case: a 10% move in enterprise value is a 25% move in the share price.

The seven conclusions that matter

  1. The 2027 earnings recovery is arithmetic, not a forecast of end markets. Adjusted EBITA rises by about SEK 80m (+25%) in 2027 from four sources of similar size, and none of the four needs an end-market recovery. About 60% to 65% of the SEK 80m is within management's control, and the Q3 2026 run-rate already shows it: underlying EBITA rose 15%, S:t Eriks held a 5% margin on sales down 9%, and Tornum's decremental margin fell to about 13%. The forecast assumes no end-market recovery before H2 2027. Because the fixed claims ahead of the ordinary shares do not grow, the 25% rise in adjusted EBITA becomes a rise of about 50% in adjusted EPS, from SEK 1.49 to SEK 2.24.
  2. The balance sheet repairs faster than the market narrative says, and that repair is the engine of the return. Leverage falls from 3.1x at Q3 2026 to about 2.7x at end-2026, as the seasonal fourth-quarter cash release arrives, and to about 2.1x at end-2027, as EBITDA grows and the ordinary dividend is cut from SEK 2.00 to about SEK 0.30. The dividend cut alone frees about SEK 135m. Once leverage is below 2.5x, around Q2 2027, the acquisition engine can restart. The point most easily missed is that the base-case re-rating is almost entirely a balance-sheet effect: at the guideline fair multiple of 11.21x two-year-forward adjusted EPS (SEK 3.57 for FY2029), the share is worth about SEK 40 at end-2027, yet the implied two-year-forward EV/EBITA is only about 10.8x, against about 10.0x today. The P/E "multiple expansion" in the DuPont split of the return is mostly the equity's share of enterprise value rising from about 40% to about 56% as debt falls and EBITA grows. Richard therefore does not need the market to fall back in love with Volati. He needs EBITDA to grow, net debt to fall, and the market not to de-rate the shares further.
  3. The forecast errors are concentrated where the earnings are not. S:t Eriks and Tornum contribute only about SEK 33m of the SEK 398m of 2027 base-case EBITA, but carry about 60% of the plausible error (from about SEK -1m combined in the bear case to about SEK +75m in the bull case; see judgement 1 below), because their margins depend on production and pricing decisions that outsiders cannot see. Corroventa's weather adds about ±SEK 15m. Because the fixed claims magnify every error, a 10% error in EBITA becomes a 17% to 20% error in adjusted EPS. The cone for 2027 adjusted EBITA runs from about SEK 330m to SEK 450m around the base of SEK 398m and is skewed down, because every ingredient of the bear case has happened at least once in the last eight quarters. The probability-weighted figure is about SEK 385m to 390m.
  4. The next four months are the fragile window, and the sequence of events decides the case. On the Q3 2026 balance sheet, an 11% fall in adjusted EBITDA with flat net debt would breach the 3.5x covenant maximum. Headroom becomes comfortable only after the fourth-quarter cash release. Management bought Tramex and NicEtikett with leverage at 2.9x to 3.1x and says it still sees attractive opportunities, so another acquisition before the FY2026 report on 11 February 2027 would reopen the balance-sheet risk. The Riksbank's November rise in its policy rate to 2.00% is already in the forecasts (a 4.6% borrowing cost), but the rise confirms that S:t Eriks' recovery belongs in 2028, not 2027.
  5. The market's picture of Volati is one broker's Hold and no investor narrative at all. DNB Carnegie (Hold, target SEK 25; adjusted EPS of SEK 1.92, 2.32 and 2.88 for 2026 to 2028) argues that leverage blocks the acquisition engine. Nordea's Buy at SEK 39 (2 October) predates the Q3 report and is stale. Our 2027 and 2028 EBITA and EPS forecasts are within 3% of DNB's, and our revenue forecasts are 2% to 4% lower in every year. The real gap between our view and the market lies in what nobody has yet articulated, on both sides of the case.

    Unarticulated positives

    • The dividend cut is a deleveraging step.
    • The acquisition restart is a story, not just a model line.
    • The H1 2027 comparisons are easy: Q1 2026 adjusted EBITA was only SEK 41m.
    • The preference shares can be redeemed: refinancing them fully with debt would add about SEK 0.36 of EPS, and a partial redemption is feasible from 2028.

    Unarticulated negatives

    • Heidelberg Materials' consolidation of Sweden's only cement supply, and its purchase of NCC's aggregates, create a structural price-cost squeeze at S:t Eriks.
    • The grain-storage price war at Tornum is structural, not cyclical.
    • The Swedish food VAT cut ends in December 2027, which hurts Ettiketto's volumes.
    • FY2026 reported ordinary EPS of about SEK 0.05, against a FactSet "consensus" of SEK 1.30, will headline the February report.
  6. The setup is not clean, which is why the fit grade is poor even though the return arithmetic is attractive. There is no guidance to beat. Estimates have been trimmed rather than capitulated. Quality is medium to low: return on capital employed including goodwill is about 8%, and margins are half the Swedish compounder median. The cause for concern, leverage, clears only if the sequence of events holds. The case most resembles Richard's "cause for concern clearing in a cyclical at trough-on-trough" setup, but in a levered, medium-quality cyclical rather than a quality one.
  7. The risk/reward is asymmetric in Richard's favour, and the timing decision is about the fragile window. The downside is more probable but smaller: the multiple already sits in the ten-year "crash" band at about 9x, and a central trough value is SEK 13 to 15. The upside is less probable but larger: SEK 40 to 48 at end-2027 if the next two reports land. Weighting the bear, base and bull cases at 30%, 50% and 20% gives an expected end-2027 value of about SEK 33 to 34, roughly +40%. The first dated test is the FY2026 report on 11 February 2027 (leverage near 2.7x, no Tornum goodwill impairment, Q4 adjusted EBITA of about SEK 82m to 85m). The second is the Q1 2027 report in late April 2027 (Q1 adjusted EBITA of about SEK 66m against SEK 41m a year earlier, and an Ettiketto margin of 14% or more after the German co-location). An investor who waits for the February report gives up perhaps SEK 3 to 5 a share of upside to avoid the fragile window; an investor who buys now is paid that SEK 3 to 5 for carrying it.

The five judgements that move the shares most, and the arithmetic if each is wrong

Three rules of thumb translate each error into the share price. SEK 10m of adjusted EBITA is about SEK 0.10 of EPS (at 22.5% tax on 79.4m shares). Base-case adjusted EPS is SEK 2.24 for 2027 and SEK 2.89 for 2028. Each 1.0x of two-year-forward P/E on FY2029 adjusted EPS of SEK 3.57 is worth SEK 3.57 a share, about 15% of the price.

The linkageJudgements 1 and 2 set the earnings; judgement 3 sets most of the return. The three are linked: a bear outcome on judgement 1 or 2 slows EBITDA growth, which slows deleveraging, which delays both the acquisition restart and the re-rating. That linkage is why the end-2027 price cone (about SEK 15 to 48) is so much wider than the 2027 earnings cone (-17% to +13%).

Grades: A 90 to 100, B 75 to 89, C 50 to 74, D 25 to 49, F 1 to 24. Scores set by the Rater.

#1Operating environment: tailwinds and headwinds

External headwinds clearly outweigh the tailwinds, and the rate cycle has just turned the wrong way, but the 2027 case is built not to need the cyclical end markets.

Evidence.

Headwinds: two cyclical platforms in falling end markets

  • Swedish construction (S:t Eriks). Building volumes are 25% to 30% below peak, housing starts are at a fraction of need, and municipal water and wastewater work began slipping in Q2 2026.
  • Rates and the consumer. Swedish consumer confidence fell from 102.3 to 94.3 in October. The Riksbank raised its policy rate to 2.00% in November 2026, and DNB expects about 2.4% by Q3 2027.
  • European farm investment (Tornum). Farm investment is frozen. The business climate index of CEMA, the European agricultural machinery association, fell to -31 in October, a 20-month low; AGCO cut its 2026 guidance; Ag Growth International's order book was down 22% at mid-year; and the supplier Componenta now treats 2027 as an interim year, with recovery in 2028.
  • Input costs. Costs are rising faster than the cyclical platforms can reprice (see the chart below): steel safeguards apply from July 2026, and freight costs are at multiples of pre-conflict levels.
  • Cement consolidation. Heidelberg Materials, Sweden's only cement producer, is consolidating clinker production at Slite and buying NCC's 106 aggregate sites for SEK 5.5bn.

Tailwinds: the stable half of the group, and easy comparisons

  • Ettiketto's demand is good. Swedish grocery sales rose 4% in Q3 on volume (Axfood); Haypp's nicotine-pouch volumes rose 33% in Q3; and the EU packaging regulation, in force since August 2026, burdens the small label converters that Ettiketto buys.
  • Communication has public-security demand. Telia's emergency-network award and Net4Mobility's SWEN framework offset a slow commercial 5G rollout (Tele2 is pushing SEK 50m to 75m of capital spending into 2027).
  • Infrastructure spending is rising. The budget of Trafikverket, the Swedish Transport Administration, is rising, and Veidekke expects Swedish civil engineering to grow 6% in both 2027 and 2028.
  • Corroventa has a first positive weather signal. Storms Austen and Boelo hit the UK in late October, after a dry Nordic autumn.
  • Comparisons become very easy from Q1 2027. In Q1 2026, S:t Eriks' adjusted EBITA was SEK -16m and Tornum's SEK -15m.

Inference. The environment is a late-cycle trough. The rate cycle has turned against the one recovery the case would most like, Swedish construction, while the stable half of the group (Ettiketto and Communication) has steady-to-improving demand. Part of Ettiketto's Swedish volume is flattered by the April 2026 cut in food VAT, which runs to December 2027, so the base effect turns negative in 2028.

So what. The base case does not need the cyclical end markets in 2027, and that independence is its strength. The base case does need the end markets in 2028 to 2030, however: about 60% of the SEK 200m of EBITA growth in those years rests on Nordic rates, through S:t Eriks, Tornum and the pace of acquisitions.

Where I differ from the market. DNB is "waiting for end markets to improve". I agree that the end markets will not improve in 2027, but I think the market under-weights two structural negatives (the Heidelberg cement squeeze, and grain-storage overcapacity that is leaving the market only slowly) and one mechanical positive (the easy H1 2027 comparisons).

Counter-case. Three signals point to an earlier recovery. Jefferies puts the bottom in agricultural equipment in late 2026 or early 2027; Ag Growth International saw orders pick up in late 2026; and Swedish inflation in October came in below expectations, which caps the Riksbank's rate path. If agriculture and rates both turn early, the 2027 bull case (adjusted EBITA of SEK 450m) comes into play.

What would change my view. A Riksbank pause combined with two consecutive quarters of rising Swedish housing starts; the CEMA index back above zero; Tornum order announcements.

Conclusion: external headwinds clearly outweigh tailwinds and the rate cycle has just turned the wrong way, but the 2027 case is built not to need the cyclical end markets.

Score: 34, set by the Rater. Two of five platforms (S:t Eriks, Tornum, about 40% of sales) face still-falling Swedish construction and frozen farm investment, a rate cycle that has just turned against them, a structural grain-storage price war and a Heidelberg cement squeeze, while Ettiketto (two-thirds of platform EBITA) and Communication have steady-to-improving demand (grocery volumes, nicotine pouches, EU packaging rules, public-security networks) and the base case assumes no end-market help before 2028; consensus sales growth of 3.7% (34th percentile) fits a clearly but not severely negative balance. I sit above the External change forces group's 27 because the headwinds hit the smaller part of the EBITA, and place it between Fevertree and Zegona.

#2Internally-driven corporate change

Volati's internal change is real, dated and mostly delivered, but it repairs a trough rather than building a new growth engine, and the people delivering 2027 have no record inside Volati.

Evidence. Five changes are complete or under way.

  • The Salix separation is done. Volati turned a SEK 500m purchase into a SEK 5.5bn listing.
  • The continuing group has been reorganised into five transparent platforms with new, operational leaders (see the panel below).
  • The cost programmes are on time. The programmes launched at S:t Eriks and Tornum in Q1 2026 show in Q3 margins, on the promised six-to-nine-month timetable. Ettiketto's German co-location of Interket (SEK 19m of restructuring costs booked in Q3) delivers savings from Q1 2027.
  • Three acquisitions in 2026 (Interket, Tramex and NicEtikett) added SEK 575m of sales.
  • The balance sheet is being repaired. The ordinary dividend is about to fall from SEK 2.00 to about SEK 0.30 (range nil to SEK 0.50), and a new SEK 3.65bn facility with Nordea and SEB, running to April 2028, removes refinancing risk.

Inference. The change is subtraction and repair, not addition: it fixes a trough rather than building a compounder. The self-help is worth about SEK 45m to 50m of adjusted EBITA in 2027 and a further SEK 20m to 25m in 2028, almost all of the 2028 amount from Ettiketto's integration work. Central costs will not contribute: head-office costs were SEK 47m for the first nine months, against SEK 44m a year earlier.

The feedback loop between leverage and acquisitions flips from balancing to reinforcing around Q2 2027. From then on, bolt-on acquisitions (SEK 50m of acquired sales in 2027 and SEK 150m to 200m a year from 2028, at margins of about 12%) add about SEK 14m of EBITA in 2028, rising to SEK 57m by 2030.

So what. The 2027 recovery rests on things management has demonstrably done before: local cost cuts, Nordic label integration, closing deals and cash-led deleveraging (as in 2021). The 2028 to 2030 path rests on something management has not yet done: lifting the margins of acquired label converters outside the Nordics (Clever is already behind plan, and Interket earns 5% to 6%), with a team assembled in one burst during a leveraged trough.

The problems. The capital-allocation philosophy is unchanged, because the CEO and the chairman are unchanged. Interket was bought at about 22x trailing EBITA, leverage was run to the ceiling into a downturn, and management's revealed preference is to buy before the balance sheet is clean. Co-founder Karl Perlhagen (39.1% of capital) left the board in November 2025 under a personal tax investigation. He has since taken the chair of both nomination committees, which argues against an imminent sale of his stake but leaves the overhang unresolved. Volati also has no internal audit function (an inventory error at S:t Eriks ran from 2016), has held no capital markets day for the continuing group, and has not quantified its cost programmes.

Where I differ from the market. DNB models 5% acquired growth from 2027 while describing acquisitions as blocked. I think the acquisition restart from H2 2027 is real and under-told, and I think the market has not noticed that the dividend cut is worth about a quarter-turn of deleveraging.

Counter-case. Three platform-CEO changes in five months, plus a new CFO, is a lot of simultaneous transition for a compact head office. The record that makes the self-help plausible was built by people who have since left or moved.

What would change my view. An acquisition announced before the FY2026 report would be negative. A capital markets day with platform margin paths and an acquisition budget would be positive; I put its probability at 30% to 40% within 18 months.

Conclusion: the internal change forces are real, dated and mostly delivered so far, but they are thinly resourced repair rather than a new growth engine, and the people delivering 2027 have no record inside Volati.

Score: 55, set by the Rater. Dated self-help is real and already showing in Q3 margins (S:t Eriks and Tornum cost programmes on the promised timetable, Ettiketto's German co-location from Q1 2027, three bolt-ons, a dividend cut freeing about SEK 135m, a refinanced facility), worth about SEK 45-50m of 2027 EBITA (about 15%) and a further 20-25m in 2028, but it is repair rather than a new engine, run by a newly assembled team, and offset by an unchanged capital-allocation habit (Interket at about 22x, leverage run to the ceiling into a downturn), no internal audit and the founder overhang. I sit above the Internal change forces group's 42 because the earnings effect is dated and evidenced, but at Richard's 'gently positive but mediocre' level, between ASML and Reply.

#3Industry structure, business model, financial profile and management

Volati is a medium-to-low quality group: its local moats are genuine, but its financial profile is weak and levered, and its best platform is being diluted by its worst two.

Industry structure and moats. Four of the five platforms are number one or two in narrow niches with rational pricing and few entrants, and those niches produced about three-quarters of 2025 platform EBITA.

  • Labels (Ettiketto): a fragmented market consolidating towards scaled converters, with switching costs embedded in customers' machines.
  • Masts (Communication): a consolidated market, protected by MAFI's patents.
  • Restoration (Corroventa): Europe's largest emergency drying fleet.
  • Precast concrete (S:t Eriks), regionally: the weight of the product makes freight costly, which creates local oligopolies.

The structural damage is confined to grain handling. Silo capacity built in 2020 to 2023 has triggered a price war (Ag Growth International is pricing commercial work "more aggressively", and Kepler Weber's gross margin is down to 16%), and Tornum, with the group's stretched balance sheet behind it, cannot win that price war by spending. There is no group-level moat: the platforms share no customers, technology or purchasing. Pricing power is, at best, cost recovery with a lag at Ettiketto (whose legacy margin is back at about 17.5%, not above it) and is negative at S:t Eriks and Tornum.

Financial profile. The group's financial profile is weak, and the capital structure magnifies the weakness. The adjusted EBITA margin was 7.7% in 2025 and is 6.7% in 2026e, against a Swedish compounder median of 13% to 16%. Return on capital employed is about 8% including goodwill and 17% excluding it (the platform returns are in the table above). Cash conversion is good at 93% on a rolling basis, although a one-off inventory release flatters it, and capital expenditure is low at about 2% of sales. Fixed claims ahead of ordinary EPS (interest of about SEK 71m, the SEK 64m preference dividend and SEK 10m of minorities) take about 46% of 2026 adjusted EBITA.

Management. Andreas Stenbäck (CEO since 2021, previously CFO) is an above-average, finance-first capital allocator and an honest communicator of misses, but he is not an operator. His one great act, the Salix separation, left the continuing group with the cyclical assets, the preference capital and leverage at the ceiling. Incentives are lean and aligned: pay of SEK 5.2m, no cash bonus, market-priced warrants and a holding of 716,433 shares; the chairman holds 18.6m shares. Governance is founder-controlled (62% of capital), and only three of the five directors are independent. Management has kept its dated operational promises in 2026, but its market-timing calls have been early for three years, and it missed its 15% target for growth in EBITA per share in 2023, 2024 and 2025.

Where I differ from the market. DNB prices Volati with the "repaired-but-unproven" acquirers: 10.7x 2027e EV/EBITA, against Storskogen at 8.4x, Sdiptech at 10.8x and Lifco at 18.1x. I agree that this is the right peer group. I would add that, weighted by normal-year EBITA, Volati's industry structure is better than the share price implies and worse than the company's marketing implies.

Counter-case. Ettiketto alone is a business of real quality: about SEK 1.75bn of sales at a 15% margin, a European consolidation runway and a proven Nordic playbook. Ettiketto is now two-thirds of the group, so a buyer of Volati today is mostly buying Ettiketto, with the cyclical platforms thrown in at a trough.

What would change my view. A disposal of S:t Eriks or Tornum at a sensible price would transform the group's quality and its multiple at once. The 2021 and 2026 precedents show that the founders are willing to separate businesses, but no disposal is signalled.

Conclusion: genuine but local moats, a weak and levered financial profile, and a capable, honest, finance-first management with too little room to act: a medium-to-low quality group whose best platform is being diluted by its worst two.

Score: 35, set by the Rater. Four of five platforms hold genuine number-one-or-two niche positions and Ettiketto is a quality business, but there is no group-level moat, pricing is lagged cost recovery at best and negative in the two cyclicals, grain handling is structurally impaired, and management is honest but finance-first with a record of buying before the balance sheet is clean; ROIC 5.9% (44th percentile), operating margin 7% (27th), ROCE including goodwill about 8% and new capital such as Interket bought at about 22x EBITA earning below its cost, with low predictability. Coherent with the groups (52, 40, 22, 40), it sits above Instalco's fragmented model and below Teqnion, close to Storskogen as its closest comparable.

#4Guidance conservatism, sell-side expectations and the delivery record

Volati gives no conservative guidance and has a poor delivery record against estimates, but the one live set of estimates is now low enough on the cyclical platforms to be beaten from April 2027 by self-help and comparison arithmetic alone.

Evidence. Volati gives no annual or quarterly guidance and has never raised or re-based a target. Its public statements fall into three groups, with very different records.

Against DNB's EBITA estimates, Volati missed five times in a row up to Q2 2026, every time in the margins of S:t Eriks and Tornum, before an in-line Q3 2026 on an underlying basis. After Q3, DNB cut its 2026 EPS by 3% to SEK 1.92, raised 2027 and 2028 by 1% to 2% (to SEK 2.32 and SEK 2.88), cut its target to SEK 25 and kept its Hold. DNB now forecasts 2027 margins of 2.6% at S:t Eriks and -1.3% at Tornum, below our 3.4% and -1.0%.

Inference. Because there is no guidance to be conservative, the test moves to the estimates. On the lines that matter, the one active broker's 2027 forecasts are now low for the cyclical platforms, and its 2028 forecasts (revenue +3%) carry almost no recovery and little acquired growth. The bar for the April and July 2027 reports is therefore low: Q1 2027 adjusted EBITA of SEK 60m to 70m, against SEK 41m a year earlier, is mostly comparison arithmetic.

So what. The classic Viewforth pattern of conservative guidance followed by serial raises is absent. Its substitute is a mechanical sequence of low-bar comparisons from April 2027, in front of a broker that has said it "would likely raise 2027 forecasts" if the Ettiketto savings land.

The trap in the February report. The published 2026 EPS forecasts sit on three different bases, as the cards below show. Reported ordinary EPS for 2026 will be about SEK 0.05, so the February 2027 report will read as a collapse to a casual reader.

Where I differ from the market. The market reads the absence of guidance as a reason for a conglomerate discount, and DNB says so. I read the dated operational statements as a form of guidance that is being met. I also see a capital markets day for the continuing group as the cheapest catalyst that management controls, and one it has not yet used.

Counter-case. A company that has missed its only target for three years, and whose CEO called the construction recovery two years early, has no claim to conservatism; its next optimistic call is as likely as its next kept promise.

What would change my view. A sixth margin miss at S:t Eriks or Tornum in Q4 2026 would weaken my view. A capital markets day that re-bases the platform targets downwards, but with dates and building blocks, would strengthen it.

Conclusion: there is no conservative guidance and the delivery record against estimates is poor, but the one live estimate set is now low enough on the cyclical platforms to be beaten by self-help and comparison arithmetic alone from April 2027.

Score: 26, set by the Rater. There is no formal guidance (neutral), but the only standing target (15% EBITA per share) has been missed in 2023, 2024 and 2025 and never re-based, EBITA missed the one broker five times in a row to Q2 2026 (by up to 35%), and the CEO called the construction recovery two years early; dated operational promises in 2026 have been kept and Q3 was in line, which lifts it a little. A record of misses this recent weighs heavily, so it sits with the Guidance (23) and Sell-side (32) groups, between Indutrade and Judges Scientific.

#5Business model leverage: pricing, operating, financial, cost-out and feedback loops

Volati's business model has strong operating and financial leverage but no pricing power, so revenue growth of 4% to 5% becomes EPS growth of 30% to 50% only while the trough is being unwound.

Pricing power: none in real terms. Price adds about 1% a year to revenue and nothing to margin. Ettiketto passes costs through with a three-to-six-month lag under index clauses; Communication's fixed-price frameworks carry no steel indexation; S:t Eriks faces a consolidated supplier (Heidelberg) and price-buying public customers; and Tornum is a price-taker in an overcapacity market. The margin recovery therefore has to be bought with cost cuts and integration, not with price.
Operating leverage: high in the cyclical platforms, and asymmetric in time. On the way down, from 2023 to 2026, group EBITA fell about 40% on sales down about 4%, because S:t Eriks and Tornum carry about 30% fixed costs and suffered under-absorption and price cuts (Tornum's decremental margin exceeded 60% in Q2 2026). On the way up, the 2027 lift comes almost entirely from removing and realigning fixed costs, not from volume. Volume leverage returns only from 2028, at incremental margins of about 30% to 35% at S:t Eriks (where each 10% of volume is worth about SEK 35m to 40m) and 20% to 25% at Tornum (where price lags volume in an overcapacity market). Ettiketto has little fixed-cost leverage; its margin moves with mix and integration.

Financial leverage: the decisive amplifier. Fixed claims below EBITA of about SEK 145m a year give adjusted EPS an elasticity to EBITA of about 2.1x in 2026, 1.7x in 2027 and 1.4x by 2030. Reported EPS, after about SEK 108m of amortisation, has an elasticity of 3.5x to 4x in 2027. The preference shares are the structural lever. They pay a dividend of SEK 40 a share on 1,603,774 shares, are redeemable at SEK 625 a share (about SEK 1.0bn in total), and cost 6.4% after tax, or about 8.2% before tax, against bank debt at about 4.5%. Refinancing the preference shares fully with debt would add about SEK 0.36 to EPS and about 1.6x to leverage; refinancing a third of them from 2028 is plausible and would add about SEK 0.12.

Cost-out scope: moderate. Beyond the programmes under way, perhaps SEK 30m to 60m more is available, mainly in procurement, but purchasing is decentralised by design and the culture resists pooling it. Plant closures would remove the spare capacity that gives S:t Eriks its recovery leverage.

Feedback loops. Six feedback loops are at work, and the balancing (self-limiting) loops dominate today. The loop that matters flips around Q2 2027: lower leverage allows bolt-on acquisitions, bolt-ons add EBITDA, and higher EBITDA lowers leverage further. Two balancing loops run through the whole forecast and cap it. The first is grain-storage overcapacity, which keeps Tornum near breakeven into 2028. The second is valuation: at this share price no equity can be issued, and the preference shares stay until about 2029. The retained cyclical platforms, which earn below the cost of capital, keep the cost of equity high throughout.

So what. Revenue growth of 4% to 5% a year in 2027 and 2028 produces adjusted EBITA growth of 25% and 16%, and adjusted EPS growth of 50% and 29%. That is the outsized profit growth Richard looks for, with one caveat: the growth runs on fixed-cost removal and fixed-claim gearing from a trough, not on pricing or a scale flywheel.

Where I differ from the market. The market sees the preference shares only as a constraint. I also see them as the clearest unmodelled EPS lever from 2028, and I see the dividend cut as the first step in the deleveraging loop flipping.

Counter-case. Leverage of this kind works equally hard in reverse: a 10% EBITA shortfall becomes a 20% EPS shortfall and pushes the deleveraging loop back towards balancing.

What would change my view. Evidence that Ettiketto can hold its prices above its costs when label-stock and freight costs fall (there is none yet); a change in management's stance on the preference shares.

Conclusion: the model has strong operating and financial leverage and a reinforcing deleveraging loop that is about to flip, but no pricing power, so revenue growth of 4% to 5% converts into EPS growth of 30% to 50% only while the trough is being unwound.

Score: 57, set by the Rater. Structurally there is no real pricing power (price adds about 1% a year and nothing to margin), operating leverage is real but asymmetric (EBITA fell about 40% on sales down 4%; the 2027 lift comes from fixed-cost removal, volume leverage of 30-35% incremental margins at S:t Eriks only from 2028, Ettiketto little), and financial leverage is the decisive amplifier (EPS elasticity to EBITA about 2.1x falling to 1.4x) but it is stretched rather than comfortable, with a deleveraging-and-bolt-on loop about to flip. Revenue growth of 4-5% becomes EPS growth of 29-50% from the trough (about five times revenue against the median twice), so the gearing is above ordinary, but held near the middle by no pricing, a stretched balance sheet and the Economic strength group's 22; the Financial forecasts group's 60 is closer.

The base case delivers four years of double-digit EBITA and EPS growth, but it is a trough recovery: 2027 is well founded, while 2028 onwards is a call on the cycle and on capital allocation.

What would change my view. Two consecutive quarters in which S:t Eriks and Tornum meet expectations (Q4 2026 and Q1 2027) would raise my confidence in the 2027 forecast to high. A third Tornum loss above SEK 10m in Q4, or an Ettiketto margin below 14% in Q1 2027, would lower it.

#7Scope for upgrades to guidance, estimates and the narrative over 6 to 12 months

Scope for upgrades is moderate and dated: 2027 estimates from April 2027 and 2028 estimates from October 2027. For the first six months, the revision screens will keep showing cuts for mechanical reasons.

Guidance. There is no guidance to raise.

Estimates: cut on the screens in February, then more likely raised than cut. At the FY2026 report in February 2027, the most likely outcome is that estimates are held in substance but cut on the screens, for three reasons.

  • Nordea's stale 2026 forecast must absorb Q3's SEK 29m of one-offs, which will pull the FactSet 2026 mean from SEK 1.30 towards about SEK 1.1.
  • The dividend consensus of SEK 0.56 will meet a proposal of nil to SEK 0.50.
  • A Tornum goodwill impairment (goodwill of SEK 139m, against book equity of about SEK 0.8bn) is a live risk at the year-end impairment test.

From April 2027, estimates are more likely to be raised than cut. I put the probability of a 2% to 6% upgrade to 2027 at about 45% at the April report and at even odds in July; a bolt-on at a sensible multiple would tip the balance. For 2028, I put the probability of a 3% to 8% upgrade from October 2027 at about 50%, because DNB's 2028 forecast contains no cyclical recovery and little acquired growth.

Narrative. Volati has one sell-side voice, DNB, and DNB has shown that it will move: it went from Buy to Not Rated to Hold within 2026. If the February and April reports land, "waiting for end markets" becomes "recovery under way", and a return to Buy is plausible. A third broker, most likely through commissioned research, has about a 40% chance of appearing within 18 months and would make the breadth-of-revisions measure meaningful.

So what. The upgrade scope is moderate and specific rather than large and diffuse: 0% to 6% on 2027 from April, 3% to 8% on 2028 from October, plus a change in the narrative. The larger prize is the multiple, which the estimate changes would unlock rather than deliver themselves.

Three near-term negatives carry no information about the business. Nordea's SEK 39 target is 60% above the price and will probably be cut, or its rating lowered, when Nordea next updates (likely within three months). FY2026 reported EPS will be near zero. A Carnegie Small Cap index reweighting is possible in December, although Volati's weight in the index is only 0.05%.

Where I differ from the market. The market's revision screen grades Volati F because it reflects the separation's mechanical halving of estimates and the mixed EPS bases. Like-for-like 2027 and 2028 estimates have stabilised and sit where ours do. The screen will nonetheless stay negative until mid-2027, whatever the operations do.

Counter-case. S:t Eriks' and Tornum's margins are set by production and pricing decisions that nobody outside the company can see, so the next miss is as likely as the next beat; five of the last six quarters missed.

What would change my view. DNB raising its 2027 forecasts in April would strengthen my view; a Q4 2026 report with S:t Eriks or Tornum below the base-case markers would weaken it.

Conclusion: scope for upgrades is moderate and dated (2027 from April 2027, 2028 from October 2027), masked for the first six months by a screen that will keep reading as cuts for mechanical reasons.

Score: 46, set by the Rater. There is no formal guidance to raise and the de facto ambitions are ignored; over 6-12 months the 2026 and dividend consensus will be cut mechanically in February (Nordea's stale figure, a possible Tornum impairment, a target cut), then 2027 has about 45% odds of a 2-6% upgrade from April and 2028 about even odds of 3-8% from October, against 25% odds of cuts and revenue growth of 4-5%, so the expected change in consensus scaled to growth is about nil to slightly positive. The narrative (one Hold, no investor story) has the most room to improve, which keeps it close to The fourth set group's 55 but below it for the negative first six months, between RELX and Tele2.

#8Current momentum: guidance, estimates, narrative, technicals, and peers

Volati's momentum is negative on every measure while its peers' momentum is strongly positive; the turn, when it comes, will be driven by Volati's own dated reports, not by the sector.

Evidence. Several of the headline readings are distorted by the Salix distribution, which removed about SEK 69 a share from the price on 15 June 2026; the table separates the clean readings from the artefacts.

Peers: the mirror image. Six of the seven peers have risen over twelve months, five of them by 40% or more. Pinned momentum ratings across the sector are mostly A and B for both technicals and estimates, and Volati is the only stock in the group rated F on both. Volati's share moves almost entirely on its own news (its six-month correlation with the sector basket is 0.13, an R-squared of 2%), so the sector's momentum has given it no support and will give none; equally, a sector de-rating would not sink it.

Inference. Momentum is negative on every axis the dashboard measures, and in the market regime that matters (risk-off, with underweights in the Fragility and Momentum factors). That negative momentum runs opposite to where the fundamental gap lies. Because Volati's multiple is driven by company events, the triggers that would turn its momentum are identifiable and dated rather than dependent on sentiment.

So what. Nobody is positioned in Volati, so there is no buyer base to respond quickly to good news. A turn in the shares would be slow and noisy, taking 12 to 18 months rather than one report.

Where I differ from the market. I agree with the screens on the facts, but I disagree that the F/F/A profile (F for technical momentum, F for earnings momentum, A for valuation) is a reason to wait indefinitely. In this framework, F/F/A is the profile at which trough-on-trough cases begin, provided the cause for concern clears.

Counter-case. In a falling market, "the cleanest case in the sector wins", and Volati is the least clean case in its sector. A momentum grade of F tends to stay F while leverage is at the ceiling and estimates are still being trimmed.

What would change my view. The price holding above its 50-day average through the February report; DNB's first upward revision; a second active broker.

Conclusion: momentum is negative on guidance, estimates, narrative and technicals, while peers' momentum is strongly positive; that pattern is the mirror image of where the fundamental gap sits, and the screens will not turn before mid-2027.

Score: 14, set by the Rater. Both measures sit in the bottom fifth, so F: estimates cut at one, three and six months (EPS -15% over six months, 10th percentile), one broker at Hold with the other's Buy stale, no narrative, and peers strongly positive but uncorrelated so giving no support. I place it in the upper part of the band because part of the revision and price readings are artefacts of the Salix distribution and mixed EPS bases, with like-for-like 2027-28 estimates broadly stable.

#9Riskiness and simplicity of the forecasts and expectations

The case is complex and levered: its 2027 direction is predictable, but its level, EPS and share price are not, and for the next four months the balance sheet is the overriding risk.

Simplicity of the case: low. The group's earnings are the sum of five low-correlation drivers (consumer labels, telecom and defence projects, floods, Swedish construction and European farm investment) less a fixed charge, with one dominant positive (Ettiketto) and two dominant negatives (S:t Eriks and Tornum). The case fails the simplicity guardrails on the number of drivers and on the number of headwinds (three of five platforms). Even the two-year-forward EPS basis needs a broker note to reconstruct.

Fragilities and requirements. The case requires five specific things to go right by mid-2027, and none of them is an end-market recovery.

Predictability. The direction of 2027 earnings is predictable, because the self-help is arithmetic. Their level is moderately predictable: the cone on 2027 EBITA is ±15%, against ±2% to 4% for proven peers. The level of EPS is poorly predictable because of the fixed claims, and the share price is unpredictable because the multiple and the capital structure set its cone. Predictability decays over the 18 months rather than improving. Up to April 2027, the reports are set by management's actions and by comparisons; from July 2027, the case depends on the deleveraging loop flipping, on Nordic rates, on the end of the food VAT cut and on an agricultural bottom that is still only a forecast.

Trackability. Disclosure is good at platform level (five segments with organic and acquired growth, margins, returns on capital and named one-offs) but poor at driver level: there is no order intake or backlog for S:t Eriks or Tornum, no size for the savings, no rental utilisation for Corroventa and no price-cost commentary. There is therefore no early warning of a backlog or weather shock. External proxies fill the gap for direction, though not for magnitude: housing starts from Statistics Sweden (SCB), Byggfakta construction data, the CEMA index, reports from Ag Growth International and Kepler Weber, rainfall from the Swedish and UK weather services (SMHI and the Met Office), volumes at Haypp and Axfood, and the preference share price as a read on dividend safety.

Sudden risks to the price, justified or not. Until the Q4 cash release, a covenant breach needs only an 11% fall in adjusted EBITDA with flat net debt. The covenant breach is the one sudden risk that is both plausible and very large; the table below sizes it alongside the others. I put the joint probability of at least one material event over 24 months at roughly one in three to one in two, because several of the risks are correlated through the same trough.

Sector and cyclical precedents. Three deleveraging precedents bracket Volati's repair, and AddLife's two-year repair on cash flow is the closest. Volati's own 2019 to 2021 cycle followed the pattern "leverage spike, margin dilution, structural divestment". In the platforms' own industries, grain-storage margins took two to three years to repair in every precedent (Kepler Weber, AGCO and Ag Growth International), and heavy building materials took until 2024 to regain their 2019 margins. The sector rule holds: a serial acquirer's multiple is the market's guess at how long its acquisition engine will run, and organic growth is the evidence. Volati's organic growth is -3%.

Fair trough value. Even a mild trough would value the shares below today's price. The mild case is about SEK 19 to 22 (10x EV/EBITA on 2027). The central case is SEK 13 to 15 (2027 EBITA cut by 10% to 15% and valued at 9.5x to 10x, equivalent to 7x to 8x adjusted EPS of SEK 1.8 to 2.0). A severe case, with leverage pressing 3.5x, is below SEK 10.

Where I differ from the market. The market treats the risk as "leverage, full stop". I see the risk as one of sequence: the same balance sheet is fragile for four months and comfortable thereafter, and the operating risk and the balance-sheet risk are a single bet on EBITDA.

Counter-case. The 2027 improvement is spread across many sources and is three-quarters within management's control; H1 2027 year-on-year growth is almost assured even in the bear case; and the bear case still delevers. Judged against Volati's own 2026 misses of 18% to 35%, a ±15% cone is progress.

What would change my view. The FY2026 balance sheet: net debt near SEK 1.2bn and leverage near 2.7x would move the balance-sheet risk from "overriding" to "ordinary".

Conclusion: a complex, levered, multi-driver case whose 2027 direction is predictable but whose level, EPS and share price are not, with a four-month window in which the balance sheet is the overriding risk and a downside cone (SEK 13 to 15) that is fatter-tailed than the operating sensitivities suggest.

Score: 16, set by the Rater. The memo's 2027 adjusted EPS cone is SEK 1.53-2.76 around 2.24 (about -32%/+23%), the case rests on five low-correlation drivers plus weather with fixed claims doubling every error, two cyclical platforms with no order or backlog disclosure carry most of the error, and an 11% EBITDA fall would breach the covenant until the Q4 cash release, with equity dilution, a goodwill impairment, a 39% holder under tax investigation and USD 0.3m a day of liquidity as sudden risks. The 2027 direction is predictable and even the bear delevers, so it sits just above the Risks group's 18 rather than at the bottom, between Instalco and Teqnion.

#10Where the stock is in its lifecycle

Fundamentally the stock is bottoming, not collapsing; the move to "turning up" depends on two dated reports, in February and April 2027.

Evidence. The dashboard's rule places the stock in the Collapsing phase, on trailing price momentum that mostly reflects the unadjusted spin-off. The fundamentals point to Bottoming instead.

  • Adjusted EBITA has stopped falling: Q3 underlying EBITA rose 15%, and last-twelve-months EBITA is about SEK 270m, against a 2026 full-year forecast of SEK 318m.
  • Estimates for 2027 and 2028 have stopped moving: ±1% to 3% over three months on a like-for-like basis.
  • The share is within 5% of its post-spin-off low.
  • The multiple is at the 3rd percentile of its five-year range and in the ten-year "crash" band.
  • Coverage and interest are at a low: one broker at Hold and no investor narrative.
  • Leverage is at its peak and about to fall.

Inference. The stock is bottoming, not collapsing. It shows the features of the end of a collapse (price, multiple and estimates have stabilised, and coverage is at a low) but not yet the first feature of turning up: a report that confirms the self-help, and a balance sheet off its ceiling. Each later phase has a named trigger. The February and April 2027 reports would confirm "turning up"; a first bolt-on and DNB moving to Buy in H2 2027 would mark "thesis broadening"; and "reinforcing" would need organic growth to turn positive at S:t Eriks and Tornum in 2028 and the preference-share option to become discussable. The step back to "collapsing" would be a covenant scare or an impairment-led hit to equity in the next four months.

Where I differ from the market. The market's 9x two-year-forward multiple prices the "stalling or turning up" phase, in which forecasts are least trusted, and the dashboard's rule says "collapsing". I say "bottoming", which the Viewforth guideline already rewards with a 20th-percentile multiple (11.21x) rather than a median one.

Counter-case. Two maxims argue against acting now: "turnarounds take longer than you think" and "name the trigger before you buy". The trigger, two good reports, has not yet happened, and five of the last six quarters disappointed. A bottom is only known after the fact.

What would change my view. A Q4 2026 adjusted EBITA below SEK 70m, or year-end leverage above 2.9x, would send the phase back to "collapsing"; a Q1 2027 report at or above the markers would move it to "turning up".

Conclusion: fundamentally bottoming (price, multiple and estimates have stopped falling, and leverage is at its peak), with the move to turning up conditional on two dated reports in February and April 2027.

Score: 44, set by the Rater. The computed Collapsing reads the unadjusted spin; the memo's Bottoming is right (underlying EBITA up 15% in Q3, like-for-like 2027-28 estimates stable, the multiple at the bottom of its range, leverage at its peak and about to fall), but there is not yet the first confirming print, momentum is F on every axis and a four-month fragile window could send it back to Collapsing. Early Bottoming with dated triggers in February and April 2027 places it just below a credible Bottoming like CVS Group.

#11The fair multiple

A two-year-forward P/E of 11.21x is fair at the 18-month horizon because deleveraging, not sentiment, earns it; 9x to 10x is fairer for the next six months, until the two dated reports land.

The guideline. Viewforth's guideline multiple for the bottoming phase is 11.21x two-year-forward P/E, the 20th percentile of the stock's own ten-year history. The current multiple is 8.87x on FactSet consensus EPS and about 9.0x on our adjusted EPS (the model's price of SEK 24.75 divided by two-year-forward adjusted EPS of about SEK 2.76), so the guideline is about 26% above the market's multiple.

My view. The guideline is fair at the 18-month horizon and slightly generous for the next six months, for four reasons.

  1. The history belongs to a different company. The ten-year range was set by a group that contained Salix (half of EBITA, steady, a 10% margin) and compounded at 12% a year with cheap capital. The continuing group is smaller, more cyclical and more levered, and has lost its diversifier, so its own historical percentiles overstate how cheap it is today. A 20th-percentile multiple is the right discount for that change; a median multiple would not be.
  2. The enterprise-value cross-check shows that 11.21x is not demanding. At SEK 40 a share at end-2027 (11.21x FY2029 adjusted EPS of SEK 3.57), the market value is about SEK 3.2bn. Adding net debt of about SEK 1.13bn, leases of about SEK 0.4bn and preference shares of SEK 1.0bn gives an enterprise value of about SEK 5.7bn: about 10.8x two-year-forward (FY2029) EBITA of SEK 530m, or about 12.3x FY2028 EBITA. The same two-year-forward EV/EBITA today is about 10.0x (SEK 4.6bn over FY2028 EBITA of SEK 462m). The P/E re-rating from 9x to 11.21x is therefore mostly the equity's share of enterprise value rising from about 40% to about 56%; the enterprise multiple barely moves. At about 10.8x, the enterprise multiple would sit where Sdiptech (10.8x) trades and well below the proven acquirers (Lifco at 18x, Addtech and Röko at 17x), which is the sector's realistic range for a repaired-but-unproven acquirer.
  3. The basis must be adjusted EPS. The guideline's history was built on FactSet consensus EPS, which for DNB adds back amortisation and deducts the preference dividend, so our adjusted EPS is the consistent basis. On reported EPS (SEK 2.38 for FY2029), 11.21x gives only about SEK 27 a share. The choice of basis is worth SEK 13 a share, and this memo states the basis explicitly so that nobody is surprised.
  4. The phase and the uncertainty justify a low multiple. For a stock that is bottoming, with forecasts whose level is only moderately predictable, a multiple at the low end of the historical range is correct. I would apply 9x to 10x until the February and April reports, 11.21x once leverage is visibly below 2.5x and the acquisition engine restarts, and 13x (the "conservative" band) only if organic growth turns positive at the cyclical platforms in 2028.

Where I differ from the market. The market pays 9x, the "crash" band, which is the right multiple for a stalling, levered cyclical. I think the stock earns the 20th-percentile multiple through deleveraging rather than through sentiment, and that the enterprise multiple needed to get there is already paid today.

Counter-case. Storskogen, which is further along its repair and has organic EBITA growth back, trades at 8.4x 2027e EV/EBITA. If the market insists on that multiple for Volati until the acquisition engine is proven, the fair P/E is about 8x to 9x FY2029 EPS, or SEK 29 to 32 a share, and the multiple's contribution to the return disappears.

What would change my view. A disposal of a cyclical platform would raise the group's quality and make a case for the median band. A covenant scare would turn the crash band from a floor into a ceiling.

Conclusion: 11.21x is a fair multiple at the 18-month horizon because it is earned by deleveraging rather than granted by sentiment (the implied forward EV/EBITA is about 10.8x, roughly where the stock trades today), but 9x to 10x is fairer for the next six months until the two reports land.

Score: 82, set by the Rater. The raw readings give A, but I move it to B because the perimeter has changed: the ten-year history and the 1.95x cohort premium belong to a group that held Salix, and RemainCo now trades at about the cohort median and at an EV/EBITA near Storskogen's, so the peer cheapness is largely deserved (neutral). Against its own range it is still cheap after allowing for that, since the memo's fair 20th-percentile multiple of 11.21x is about 26% above today's 9x, so I place it in the upper half of B.

#12Total shareholder return, DuPont

The indicative total return is +63% to end-2027 at the guideline multiple, about half from geared earnings growth and half from a re-rating that is in substance deleveraging; weighted for a 30% chance of a bear case at SEK 15, the expected return is about +40%.

Indicative figures
The returns below are indicative calculations on the corrected adjusted EPS at the model's price of SEK 24.75, and must be confirmed when the model is re-run with the corrected input, a continuing-operations base and the preference dividend deducted. At today's SEK 23.75, each return is about four points higher. The model summary's +272% (18-month horizon) and +335% (three-year horizon) are artefacts and must not be used; the end notes show them so that they can be recognised.

The 18-month horizon (31 December 2027, 14 months away). Two-year-forward adjusted EPS at that date is FY2029's SEK 3.57, which at 11.21x gives SEK 40.0 a share. Adding the SEK 0.30 ordinary dividend paid in 2027 gives a value of about SEK 40.3 and a total return of about +63% (about +47% annualised). In the multiplicative DuPont split, earnings contribute +29% (two-year-forward EPS rising from about SEK 2.76 to SEK 3.57), the multiple +25% (from about 9.0x to 11.21x) and dividends about +1%.

The three-year horizon (30 June 2029). FY2030 adjusted EPS of SEK 4.22 at 11.21x, plus SEK 1.60 of dividends (SEK 0.30, 0.55 and 0.75), gives a value of about SEK 48.9 and a return of about +98% (about +29% a year). Earnings contribute +53%, the multiple +25% and dividends about +6%.

What drives the return, in order of importance.

  1. Deleveraging dressed as a multiple. As #11 shows, about 25 points of the 63% come from the P/E moving from 9x to 11.21x, but in enterprise terms that move is less than one turn of EV/EBITA. The real driver is net debt falling from SEK 1.33bn to about SEK 1.13bn while EBITA rises from SEK 318m to SEK 530m: the equity captures all of the growth in enterprise value and some of the debt's former share.
  2. Fixed claims gear up EPS growth. The 29-point earnings contribution comes from two-year-forward EBITA growth of under 20% (from a FY2027 and FY2028 blend of about SEK 450m to FY2029's SEK 530m), geared up by interest, the preference dividend and minorities, none of which grows.
  3. Self-help drives 2027; the cycle and acquisitions drive the years after. About 60% to 65% of the first SEK 80m of EBITA growth is within management's control; about 60% of the next SEK 200m depends on Nordic rates.
  4. Dividends are immaterial (about 1% to 6% of the return), a direct consequence of the dividend cut and of the preference shares' seniority.

The probability-weighted cone. At end-2027, the bear case is about SEK 15 (two-year-forward EPS of about SEK 1.9 at 8x; 30% probability), the base case about SEK 40 (50%) and the bull case about SEK 48 (FY2028 bull-case EPS of about SEK 3.7 at 13x; 20%). The expected value is about SEK 33 to 34, a return of about +40% against SEK 23.75. The distribution has the classic leveraged-trough shape: the downside is more likely but shallower in price, because the multiple is already at a floor band, while the upside is less likely but larger, because a 15% rise in enterprise value is a 35% rise in the ordinary equity.

When the return is earned. The first six months carry mostly risk events and little return: the November rate rise (already delivered) and the February report, with its near-zero reported EPS, dividend reset and impairment test. Months 6 to 18 carry the comparison arithmetic, the deleveraging loop flipping and the first possible upgrades, and are when most of the 63% would be earned. The three-year horizon adds the acquisition restart and the preference-share option. The option is not in the base case and is worth about SEK 0.12 to 0.36 of EPS, or SEK 1.3 to 4.0 a share at 11.21x.

Where I differ from the market. DNB's SEK 25 target is a Hold on today's leverage and does not roll forward to a deleveraged 2027 balance sheet. The gap between SEK 25 and SEK 40 is almost entirely balance-sheet mechanics and the choice of forward year, not a different view of earnings.

Counter-case. On reported EPS, the same arithmetic gives SEK 27 (+9%); on Storskogen's multiple, SEK 29 to 32 (+20% to +30%); and in a bear case on both earnings and the multiple, SEK 15 (-37%). The +63% requires the market to accept adjusted EPS as the basis and the balance sheet to follow the base-case path.

What would change my view. The re-run of the model; the FY2026 net debt figure; a change in management's stance on the preference shares.

Conclusion: an indicative +63% to end-2027 (+98% over three years) at the guideline multiple, about half from fixed-claim-geared earnings growth and half from a P/E re-rating that is in substance deleveraging, with a probability-weighted return of about +40% once a 30% bear case at SEK 15 is allowed for.

Score: 90, set by the Rater. About +40% maps to about 91, and I move it to the floor of A for the fat, correlated lower tail (a 30% bear at SEK 15), a return that depends on the market accepting adjusted EPS (on reported EPS it is about +9%) and a deleveraging re-rating, and indicative figures still to be confirmed by the re-run.

#13Summary conclusion on the business and its investment case

Volati today is a levered remainder of five platforms. Its best business, Ettiketto, is diluted in the reported numbers by two cyclical platforms at the bottom of their cycles; its ordinary equity is a 40% slice of the enterprise, behind SEK 2.7bn of debt, leases and preference capital; and its market consists of one broker at Hold and no investors talking about it.

The case for

The case for the shares does not depend on the end markets turning. It rests on four links:
  • About SEK 80m of 2027 EBITA improvement is already arithmetic.
  • The fixed claims double that improvement in EPS.
  • Leverage falls from 3.1x to about 2.1x on EBITDA growth, seasonal cash and a dividend cut.
  • At a 20th-percentile multiple, the equity's rising share of a slowly growing enterprise value is worth about SEK 40 by end-2027, against SEK 23.75 today.

The case against

The case against the shares also has four parts:
  • The forecast errors sit in the weather and in the two platforms that earn less than a tenth of 2027 EBITA.
  • The balance sheet is fragile until 11 February 2027, and management likes to buy before the balance sheet is clean.
  • Nothing in the structure helps the market see the recovery when it comes: there is no guidance, no capital markets day, two EPS bases and a reported EPS near zero.
  • The end-2027 price cone is wide, at SEK 15 to 48.
The practical questionThe fundamental outcomes are skewed down, the price outcomes are skewed up, and the two dated tests come in February and April 2027. The practical question for Richard is therefore not whether the arithmetic works, but how much of the fragile window to carry in exchange for a better price.

End notes

Definitions. "Adjusted EBITA" is before items affecting comparability and before amortisation of acquired intangibles. "Adjusted EPS" is earnings per ordinary share after the SEK 64m preference dividend and minorities, and before amortisation. "Reported EPS" also deducts amortisation and one-offs. Leverage is on the company's definition (net debt excluding leases, divided by adjusted EBITDA after lease costs) unless stated. The Salix Group distribution of 15 June 2026 was made under the Swedish Lex Asea rules for tax-neutral spin-offs. "The continuing group" (RemainCo) is Volati after that distribution.

Prices. The memo uses SEK 23.75 (23 October 2026). The Financial Analyst's model used SEK 24.75 (22 October 2026), and the returns in #12 are measured against that model price.

The forecasts of record. The Financial Analyst's model summary (update 2) shows FY2027 EPS of SEK 6.11 and a total return of +272%. Those figures are artefacts of three mechanical faults: quarterly growth applied to pre-spin-off quarters, a pre-spin-off opening working capital, and no deduction of the preference dividend or minorities. The third forecast set documented the three faults and wrote the corrective input. The forecasts this memo uses are the second forecast set's cross-check, which the model reproduces once corrected: adjusted EBITA of SEK 318m, 398m, 462m, 530m and 597m for 2026 to 2030, and adjusted EPS of SEK 1.49, 2.24, 2.89, 3.57 and 4.22. The return figures in #12 are the third set's indicative calculation on that basis and must be confirmed by the re-run of the model.

Bases. All forecasts are the memo's corrected base case, for continuing operations after the Salix distribution of 15 June 2026. Returns are indicative and are to be confirmed by the re-run of the model.

Visuals not shown. Three default visuals are left out because they carry the uncorrected model summary or the pre-spin-off perimeter: the financial trajectory chart and the Viewforth-against-consensus table show the uncorrected Viewforth forecasts (for example FY2027 EPS of SEK 6.11), and the ten-year financials table repeats the annual history and consensus tables shown in #6. The default total-return chart is shown above only to identify the artefact.

Drawn visuals. Charts in visuals/drawn and visuals/drawn-copy-editor take their figures from the memo. Where a figure is computed rather than stated (the shares of platform EBITA in #3, the 2026 EPS bridge in #4, the growth rates in #5, the 2026 to 2030 EBITA bridge in #6 and the SEK split of the DuPont in #12), the note under the chart says so.

Default visuals. The price, valuation, momentum, revision and peer charts are the Master Dashboard's and FactSet's; the five financial tables are Richard's standard tables from FactSet. Price-based readings before 15 June 2026 are unadjusted for the distribution.

How to read this page

Every rating of this stock on one page: the Rater's 1-100 number, its letter and the Rater's own reason (at most three sentences, taken from the ratings file; nothing newly written). The number is the company's approximate standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10; 50 = typical). A letter follows its item's rule: rank among the stocks scored (A the top 10%; B+ and B the next 15%; C+, C and C- the next 25%; D the next 25%; F the bottom 25%); or Richard's cut-offs on the measure for the four numerical topics (forecast financials, current momentum, the fair multiple, total shareholder return). On the change-forces items the number carries a sign (50 = neither positive nor negative) and the letter is the rank, so read the two together. "9th of 30 stocks scored" is the stock's place on that item. A dashed badge is provisional (fewer than 30 stocks scored).
